root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: St. Petersburg Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 b6

overview: Black develops the queen's bishop to b7 to control e4, with 5.Nf3 Bb7 6.Bd3 O-O 7.O-O the usual continuation. White develops harmoniously and may take on c3 or play a3 and Qc2 or Ne5, while Black fights for e4 with ...Ne4 or ...d5 and ...Bxc3 at the right moment. Play is positional with piece manoeuvring and the e4 square as the focal point.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3, Bd3 and O-O, with Ne5 or Qc2 ideas.
Seek the bishop pair if Black plays ...Bxc3 and build a central majority.

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 with ...Bb7 and ...Ne4 or ...d5 and ...Bxc3.
Double White's pawns with ...Bxc3 when it helps.

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d4/e3 with possible doubled c-pawns after ...Bxc3, against ...b6/...Bb7.

character.notes: Positional manoeuvring around e4, without forcing tactics.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; tension around e4, d5 and c4.

level.notes: Piece placement and pawn structure matter more than memorised lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.Bd3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 b6 5. Bd3
sublines_that_differ.how: Delays Nf3 and keeps Ne2 options.

character.reason: Positional and not forcing, but Black has dynamic counterplay.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension around e4 and d5.

level.reason: Structural understanding matters more than memorisation.

plans.reason: Black may give up the bishop for doubled c-pawns, White gets the pair.
